text.title: Retro Format Rotation Guide Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every retro format rotation guide application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: `last_3_formats` MUST be read from the three most recent committed retro instances for this team (newest first), each naming its format and its action-item and participant counts. History reconstructed from memory or chat is invalid. With fewer than three committed instances the guide MUST NOT emit a `next_format`; it records `skip: history < 3` instead.

rationale.source: Widely established practice in evidence-based process improvement

rule.rationale: Facilitators remember the retro they enjoyed, not the one they ran. A rotation built on "I think we did sailboat last time" picks the same format twice in four cycles and nobody notices until participation is already gone. Three committed instances is the minimum for the no-repeat rule to mean anything.

rule.statement: `next_format` MUST be one of the seven supported formats (`start-stop-continue`, `sailboat`, `4ls`, `timeline`, `anonymous-async`, `mad-sad-glad`, `lean-coffee`) and MUST NOT appear anywhere in `last_3_formats`. The only exception is an `async` team whose async-capable pool is exhausted (see `r-async-team-rotates-within-async-pool`), and that exception MUST be recorded in the rationale.

rationale.source: Derby and Larsen, Agile Retrospectives (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2006); Retromat activity library

rule.rationale: Retro fatigue sets in within four to six cycles of the same format: the third column empties, the same three complaints recur, action items dry up. Four distinct formats in any four consecutive retros is the cheapest structural guarantee against that, and it removes the "what format this time?" debate from every planning conversation.

rule.statement: When `team_state.distribution` is `async`, `next_format` MUST be run with anonymous asynchronous input: either `anonymous-async` or `sailboat`, `4ls`, `start-stop-continue` or `timeline` on a shared board with a collection window spanning every timezone. `mad-sad-glad` and `lean-coffee` MUST NOT be picked for an `async` team. If every async-capable format is in `last_3_formats`, the guide picks the one used longest ago and records the exception.

rationale.source: Widely established practice in distributed-team facilitation; GitLab Handbook, asynchronous communication guidance

rule.rationale: Rotating an async team onto lean-coffee "for variety" gives the overlap-hour timezone a retro and everyone else a summary. Distribution is a harder constraint than novelty; the rule makes the async pool explicit so the no-repeat rule cannot push a team into a format that structurally excludes half of it.

rule.statement: A format is stale for a team when any of the following holds: it appears twice in `last_3_formats`; the action-item count dropped by more than 50% between two consecutive retros that used it; or the most recent outcome review recorded two or more participants who contributed nothing. A stale format MUST be excluded from the next pick even if it is otherwise not in the last three, and the detector's triggering signal MUST be named in the rationale.

rationale.source: Derby and Larsen, Agile Retrospectives (2006), on reading the room; widely established practice in agile coaching

rule.rationale: The no-repeat rule catches repetition; it does not catch a format that stopped working after one use. A sailboat retro that produced one action and two silent developers is stale after a single run, and the count-based detector is what lets a solo PM see that without a coach in the room.

rule.statement: When `team_state.fatigue_signal` is `fatigued`, `next_format` MUST be a format this team has not used in the last 12 months, or has never used, and the rationale MUST state when it was last used. When it is `rotating`, the no-repeat rule alone applies. `fresh` teams MAY use the in-person tie-breakers (sailboat or lean-coffee for `in-person`, `4ls` for a reflective mid-cycle need).

rationale.source: Widely established practice in agile facilitation (retro fatigue); Retromat activity library

rule.rationale: A fatigued team does not need the fourth-most-recent format, it needs one it has no muscle memory for. Forcing the 12-month lookback is what keeps rotation from becoming a four-format loop that is itself a routine.

rule.statement: `rationale` MUST be at least 20 characters and MUST name all three previous formats, the `distribution`, the `fatigue_signal`, and which tie-breaker or exception decided the pick. "Everyone likes it", "seemed right", or a rationale that does not mention team state is rejected.

rationale.source: Derby and Larsen, Agile Retrospectives (2006), choosing activities per context

rule.rationale: The rationale is what the next facilitator, or the same PM in six months, reads to learn whether the pick was a decision or a habit. Without the named tie-breaker the quarterly health check cannot tell whether the rotation refreshed signal or simply changed the column headings.

rule.statement: For every retro this guide schedules, the outcome review MUST record the format actually run, the number of action items produced, the number of participants, and the number who contributed nothing. A rotation guide whose last two scheduled retros have no recorded counts is invalid: the stale-format detector has no data and the next pick MUST NOT be emitted until the counts are backfilled.

rationale.source: Deming PDCA cycle; widely established practice in operating-cadence review

rule.rationale: Every detector in this guide is count-based. Without the counts the rotation is a random walk through seven formats, and the PM will not learn that action items halved until the team stops showing up.

rule.statement: At each outcome review the guide MUST compare the scheduled retro's action-item count and contributing-participant count against the previous retro. If two consecutive rotations to a non-stale format both fail to raise either count, the guide MUST record `fatigue is not a format problem` and route the signal to the team-health methodology (morale pulse or burnout tripwires) instead of picking a third format; further rotation is suspended until that review is done.

rationale.source: Derby and Larsen, Agile Retrospectives (2006); widely established practice in team-health diagnostics

rule.rationale: Rotating through five formats while participation keeps falling is treating a morale problem with stationery. The guide's job is to detect when the format is no longer the variable, and the two-rotation limit is what stops a solo PM from spending a quarter on the wrong lever.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit an artefact passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions hold.

rule.statement: Skip; surface the missing precondition; do not synthesize.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.
